textPlacement.assessment: Both new age contexts preserve watching beside an available adult, optional practice and gradual participation without requiring a young toddler to speak or join.
Both contexts retain the sibling unit’s closeness, optional involvement, acceptance of difficult feelings and immediate adult protection without assigning a fixed toddler age.
Both contexts preserve neutral support, protection from harm and adult-provided ideas for younger or preverbal children, without requiring equal attention or a close sibling friendship.
Both contexts allow gestures and adult-supplied solutions for younger toddlers while retaining the source’s acknowledgment, collaborative problem solving and immediate safety limits.
Both contexts retain the distinction between mainly parallel play before about two and a half and possible shared play later, with supported waiting, protected ongoing use and public courtesy.
Both contexts preserve shared attention, preparation and opportunities for movement in public places without inventing a length of time a toddler should wait.
Both contexts preserve the optional shoulder-hand signal, adult acknowledgment and response at an appropriate pause while keeping urgent help outside the waiting convention.
Both contexts preserve attention to welcome or withdrawal during ordinary affection alongside the adult’s responsibility for necessary gentle care and immediate protection.

The new body and both topic rows preserve mainly parallel play before about two and a half, possible earlier sharing with regular peers, mutually welcome shared play, adult protection and the source’s public-place exception without making shared play a deadline.
